sol.problem:
A matched non-permutation computation/adjoint on clean workspace is never recognized as restoring its known-zero entry before a subsequent borrow frame. Memoryless ptr_width=32 signature: {"abi":"0.8","args":[],"bounds":[],"in":[],"kind":"action","mem":[],"mut":[1],"tier":"q"}. Exact function (LF after every line):
action @a (t:wire mut) () () () ()
^entry():
c = qalloc any 1
h c
h c
b = qborrow any 1
cx c b
qreturn b
qfree c
Store interface/closure H=12efae749cb84eec0918c9aa49adb348957eba9e81e0eaa8f2514481a0d9dba0 in the usual sole symbol 0; with the canonical 0.8 header, section symbols, blank line and section functions, object_hash=b2534762bf5eb795efd7ba74195198f0b67e2012b9f3243700e58ee92ee9fc53. Independently built those bytes and hashes with Python, without Object::parse. check and run-action /dev/stdin a --mut 0 both exit 1, empty stdout, '§5.6: a wire released inside a borrow frame is not clean'. Hand: H^2=I, so c=0 before CX; CX(0,b)=I for every unknown b and any entangled reference, and c is freed clean. The entire action is identity on t and bR. factorises replays each Other(H c) by replacing c with a new unrelated Boolean variable, so the second H cannot restore c=0. This is a definite rejection, not an unresolved opaque claim. No token or execution budget is involved.
sol.fix: Change reference-interpreter/src/borrow.rs::Compiler::compile/Node::Other and factorises entry-context plumbing, or reuse sound matched-computation facts from the §6 analysis. Record sufficient quantum operation/control-version information to recover established facts after a matched computation and adjoint, rather than irrevocably forgetting a touched allocation. Keep the actual non-permutation frame boundaries and the full-domain borrowed-system checks. §5.3's adjoint table says 'h ... self-adjoint'; §6.2 says '`other` values are released only by the adjoint of the sequence that produced them'; §14.2 says '`qalloc` tensors |0⟩'; §5.6 requires 'P_F = P′ ⊗ I_B'. Here the entry constraint to the CX frame is exactly c=0 and its realized operation is identity. Add r7_restored_zero_before_borrow to tests/r1_borrow.rs and the exact object above to tests/cli_xam.rs. Before the fix parse/check fails; afterwards parse/hash/check must succeed with the pinned hashes, run-action for --mut 0 and 1 must return respectively state {"0":[1,0]} and {"1":[1,0]}, and --state '0=0.6,0;1=0,0.8' must be preserved. Independently start both forward and adjoint, require one surviving interface wire and reverse equals_entry=true. In the library use a supplied b entangled with an untouched reference and require exact identity on bR. No budget is needed. Include the empty-borrow variant and other matched non-permutation adjoints, while retaining the single-H dirty-control and single-X-b rejection tests; do not resolve this by treating uncertainty as proof or requiring a certificate for this identity.

sol.problem:
The non-permutation qloop route emits only n.min(3) copies. With the new round-6 prefix replay, that truncated circuit supplies incorrect reachable entry facts, and an invalid borrowed operation is admitted. Memoryless ptr_width=32 signature: {"abi":"0.8","args":[],"bounds":[4],"in":[],"kind":"action","mem":[],"mut":[1],"tier":"q"}. Exact function:
action @a (t:wire mut) () () () ()
regs {  } bounds {4}
^entry():
c = qalloc any 1
x c
qloop 4 {
h t
x c
}
b = qborrow any 1
cx c b
qreturn b
h t
x c
qfree c
Interface/closure H=232f157c4fe6c4abdb3ebc384d1b19b01751b68df4949b86d25996e87c300515; stored-H object_hash=3e8f134a472e3e31545e6bd3ec22058da463927ea24af3929bf3357a36ca3926 (canonical sole-symbol object, independently hashed). check /dev/stdin exits 0/status ok. run-action /dev/stdin a --mut 0 then exits 1, empty stdout, '§5.6: borrowed wires were not returned to their entry state'. Hand: c starts at 1 and four X operations leave c=1; the one CX flips b, violating restoration for every b. The trailing X restores c and the disjoint trailing H does not repair b. The checker instead replays three X operations, infers c=0 at this borrow, and admits it. The reverse-direction error is observable too: remove the initial x c and both trailing h t / x c, leaving qfree c; the true four-iteration action is identity but check rejects it as unclean. That positive has H=fe26a45f4d75fde7d13f0e915a13d15a6ab9bb6b280dcc302996df1391f899d9 and object_hash=7f1312cd66fc88f5819be157a1a5964c27363f8f1bc728a9b21cdb342685b198. No token/budget or certificate is involved. Repeating frame shapes is not sufficient to repeat their carried entry values.
sol.fix: Replace the n.min(3) approximation in reference-interpreter/src/borrow.rs::Compiler::compile with a sound structured treatment of non-permutation loops and their carried state, and update Object::decide_frames/factorises to consume that treatment. A valid cycle summary or composition must preserve entry facts at every actual lifetime/return and the actual final state; examining first/junction/last shapes alone cannot establish these facts. Preserve existing scalable loop behavior, independent borrow lifetimes and the permutation-only touch guard; do not introduce a trip-count restriction. §4.6 defines qloop as 'body n times'; §5.6 says the completed operation is the declared operation '⊗ identity on every borrowed bundle and on any external system entangled with it'; §5.7 transformations 'MUST produce on every x ∈ D the same final interface tuple'. Add r7_nonpermutation_loop_carried_borrow_context in tests/r1_borrow.rs and tests/cli_xam.rs with BOTH exact subjects above. Currently the negative parses/checks successfully and the positive is rejected. After the fix the negative must fail Object::parse and CLI hash/check with exit 1, empty stdout and §5.6, before execution. The positive must parse/hash/check successfully, preserve t=0/1 and 0.6|0>+0.8i|1> in each independently started direction, leave no workspace, preserve an externally entangled borrowed input and reverse with equals_entry=true. Both tests need no budget. Add a four-times alpha-renamed unrolling, nested 2×2 loops, counts 3/4/5/8 and explicit initial c=0/1 controls, with expected restoration determined by c_at_borrow = initial_c XOR (n mod 2). Retain prior per-return and certificate negatives.

sol.section: §§4.4, 4.6, 14.2 and README run-action contract; reference-interpreter/src/exact.rs::Dyadic::to_f64, Root2::to_f64, Amplitude::approximate; src/main.rs::action_state_json
sol.fix: Change reference-interpreter/src/exact.rs::Dyadic::to_f64 to convert the combined numerator/denominator using a bounded mantissa and the net binary exponent, with correct handling of rounding and subnormals. The scaled conversion already used in src/exact/measurement.rs is a useful shared primitive; avoid separately materializing an overflowing integer and underflowing scale. Ensure Root2::to_f64/Amplitude::approximate also keep a finite representable result finite rather than masking NaN or clamping it. §14.2 says 'gates act by §4.4 under the active predicate'; §4.4 fixes H=(1/sqrt(2))[[1,1],[1,-1]] and T=diag(1,e^{iπ/4}); §4.6 says 'body n times'. README.md promises run-action state contains 'the binary64 values of the exact amplitudes'. Therefore the exact state above must be reportable with exit 0. Add an internal exact.rs unit test with n=2^2000+1, k=2000: Dyadic {n,k}.to_f64() must equal 1.0 (the correctly rounded value of 1+2^-2000), whereas the current conversion is non-finite. Add the exact action to tests/cli_xam.rs: --mut 0, no budget, must exit 0 with wires=1, mut=[null], exactly keys 0 and 1 and the four finite coordinates above within 1e-12, preserving their phases and unit norm. Include standalone --adjoint and reverse equals_entry=true. The expected state is the specified matrix product, not a second run of the interpreter; retain exact-support/nonzero and measurement tests. Do not impose a gate-count/denominator ceiling or weaken float_json's rejection of actually non-finite inputs.

codex.problem:
Borrow validation silently replaces a loop containing a non-permutation gate with at most three body copies, although the new prefix replay makes later frame validity depend on the evolving loop entry. Exact memoryless ptr_width=32 signature: {"abi":"0.8","args":[],"bounds":[4,4],"in":[],"kind":"action","mem":[],"mut":[1],"tier":"q"}. Function:
action @a (t:wire mut) () () () ()
regs {  } bounds {4, 4}
^entry():
c = qalloc any 4
x c[0]
qloop 4 {
h t
b = qborrow any 1
cx c[3] b
qreturn b
h t
swap c[3] c[2]
swap c[2] c[1]
swap c[1] c[0]
}
qloop 4 {
h t
swap c[1] c[0]
swap c[2] c[1]
swap c[3] c[2]
h t
}
x c[0]
qfree c
Independent interface/closure H=5dcd11b58f335ac7f301caf4e2773ffbfb172a01330fdb6c7c990c15036b340f; with that stored H, object_hash=d58420852a90bad7d351d52072827bff5c6a8b592ae25072cffdf3b793e88de3. CLI hash and check exit 0/status ok. run-action /dev/stdin a --mut 0, run-action with --mut 1 --adjoint, and reverse a --mut 1 exit 1 with empty stdout and '§5.6: borrowed wires were not returned to their entry state'. Hand: c starts at integer 1 and its three swaps rotate the one to positions 1,2,3,0. Therefore c[3] at the four CX instructions is 0,0,0,1: the fourth fresh borrowed entry beta is returned as beta XOR 1. H(t) pairs are identity, the second loop restores c, and the final X makes c clean. The object must be rejected under §5.6 before hash/check produce output. Replacing both trip counts by 3 is valid identity and succeeds. Replacing both by 8 (signature/bounds [8,8]) is still invalid at returns 4 and 8, but check, run-action and reverse ALL succeed, with equals_entry=true: later restoration hides the violated lifetimes. Its H=4036a594dfa32ab65353367719970549a2cbe1237e471ff6f43b169e09844112 and object_hash=bc9ac8d642fe4c4569d81021da302108919d500fda82cde3577a2916b681068c. A canonical four-iteration alpha-renamed unrolling rejects correctly with §5.6. No execution budget or certificate is involved.
codex.fix: Change src/borrow.rs::Compiler::compile's qloop representation and the factorises/decide_frames transfer so every executed iteration's reachable entry and every dynamic return obligation is represented. §4.6 defines qloop as 'body n times'; §5.1 requires 'every qborrow by a qreturn after its frame'; §5.6 requires the frame to factor as 'P_F = P′ ⊗ I_B' and the completed operation to be identity on borrowed/external systems. The first three frame shapes are not a proof of all later entry states. Retain the actual trip count and compose an entry-state/obligation transfer, or use another exact traversal with a proved cycle summary; do not fix this by rejecting all larger loops or dropping established clean facts. Add the literal four-trip function using support::borrow_lifetime_object(body, &[4,4]).replace("perm_action", "action") in tests/r1_borrow.rs: assert Object::parse is Err with §5.6. In tests/cli_xam.rs use the supplied stored H and require hash/check exit 1, empty stdout and §5.6; these assertions fail now. Repeat for trips 5 and 8 and nested/renamed unrollings; even global identity at 8 must reject. For the positive [3,3] subject, require parse/check success and complete identity on all t/b basis entries, superposition and b entangled with a reference, independently forward and adjoint. Keep the existing large-bound valid-loop tests; introduce no semantic trip-count cap. For invalid cases a certificate must not waive the fourth/eighth return.

codex.problem:
The boundary repair preserves facts only on untouched wires, and incorrectly destroys a known basis value on a diagonal operand or read-only quantum control. Exact memoryless ptr_width=32 signature: {"abi":"0.8","args":[],"bounds":[],"in":[],"kind":"action","mem":[],"mut":[1],"tier":"q"}. Function:
action @a (t:wire mut) () () () ()
^entry():
c = qalloc any 1
s c
b = qborrow any 1
cx c b
qreturn b
sdg c
qfree c
Independent interface/closure H=0d7a3eccbc3cdd7440ec3c1ad66a12e8650203486b2736f6fe5ea2ddb87a56f6; stored-H object_hash=5b407065c615539c15c7f9381b8fccfebc8e109cae3e8966c05fbd4acd687205. hash, check, run-action a --mut 0, standalone adjoint with --mut 1, and reverse a --mut 1 all exit 1 with empty stdout and '§5.6: qreturn does not restore borrowed wire v2_0'. Hand: qalloc sets c=0; S|0>=|0>; CX(c,b) is identity for every unknown b and external reference; Sdg leaves c clean. The complete action is I, including phase. Removing S/Sdg accepts and runs/reverses as identity. Compiler emits S as Other([c]); prefix replay replaces c=0 with a free variable, inventing an invalid qreturn branch. Independently, replacing S/Sdg by the prefix 'qpred c; h t; qunpred c' (one instruction per line, before qborrow, no trailing gate) is also identity because c=0 disables H, but check rejects 'a wire released inside a borrow frame is not clean'. Its H=06b70e4ca0799aac622c280b3f1de5b825888d21c19da5ec3f015c88b4fc1fe6. The control is included in Other's touched set and wrongly invalidated. This extends beyond the disjoint-wire round-6 examples, which are fixed.
codex.fix: Change src/borrow.rs::Compiler::compile and the Node::Other/factorises state-transfer plumbing to distinguish all touched wires from outputs whose computational-basis information is changed. §4.3 defines qalloc as 'n clean wires'; §4.4 gives S=diag(1,i); §6.1 says 'diagonal gate on u | unchanged'; §14.2 says qalloc tensors |0⟩ and qfree removes clean factors. A diagonal operation must retain c=0, and a control operand must retain its basis value. Continue to partition frames at non-permutation gates and use the FULL touched set for §5.6's rule that borrowed wires are touched 'as control or target' only inside permutation-only frames; do not reclassify S as a permutation or admit S on b. Preserve appropriate phase/cleanup obligations separately. Add the literal function to tests/r1_borrow.rs and tests/cli_xam.rs with the supplied hash: Object::parse, hash and check must succeed; run-action at t=0/1 and a complex superposition must output the identical state with one interface wire; standalone adjoint must do the same; reverse must report equals_entry=true. The parse-success assertion fails now. Use support::r6_map(&object, false), or an equivalent independently expected I_t ⊗ I_bR check, to cover arbitrary/entangled borrowed entry state. Add the known-zero controlled-H variant as another positive, and retain negatives with X c before a single CX, a genuinely changed non-diagonal c, and any non-permutation gate touching b, even when a certificate is attached. No budget or certificate should be needed for either positive.
